long_description:
THE KEEPER OF CAPE VESPERS — an original YA survival thriller short film (12 min).

Iris Vaughn, 22, takes a seasonal job as the relief keeper of an automated lighthouse on Cape Vespers, a small island in the Salish Sea, where her aunt Marisol died the previous winter. The official report said it was a fall. Iris came to grieve. Then she lifted a buckled kitchen floorboard and found her aunt's hidden journal — written in a code Marisol had taught Iris at twelve — and learned that someone had been coming to the island on Thursdays for forty years, that the lighthouse inspector was paid to look the other way, and that her aunt's death was not an accident.

As a storm closes the island, Iris must decide: escape with the evidence, or stay and rig the long-decommissioned fog-signal whistle to broadcast the keeper's SOS pattern across the storm — the pattern her aunt taught her, on the same rainy afternoon she taught her the code.

The film is built from three structural lessons drawn from classic public-domain survival fiction (Poe's 'Pym,' London's 'The Scarlet Plague,' Wells's 'Moreau'): the escalation ladder, the frame-narrative voice of a survivor who has lost someone, and the midpoint reveal as a moral fact rather than a monster. None of the reference works' content is reproduced; only general narrative techniques are learned from them.

All imagery is original AI-generated artwork, hand-prompted scene-by-scene in a consistent cinematic Pacific Northwest visual style. Narration is synthesized via AI text-to-speech. The story, screenplay, character identities, setting, and antagonist are entirely original.
